citation.source: Computed from IUPAC standard atomic weights (Na 22.98977, Cl 35.453) — identical to salt.json's own citation. Chemically the same substance as table/kosher salt; flaky sea salt is a real, distinct PRODUCT by crystal structure and real-world USE, not composition.
citation.note: Per-gram sodium content is identical to salt.json/kosher_salt.json — see domainFacts.gramsPerTeaspoon below for the real, structured volume difference.

citation.source: Convergent culinary/reference sources on Maldon-style flaky sea salt (aqua-calc volume-to-weight data; convergent consumer culinary sources independently checked) — roughly a third to half the density of fine table salt
citation.note: The widest real crystal-size effect of the three salt entities in this repo (compare salt.json's 6g/tsp, kosher_salt.json's 3-5g/tsp) — large, hollow, pyramidal flakes trap the most air of any of the three. Sources checked this session disagreed on the exact figure by roughly 2x (some citing ~2g/tsp, one cup-weight-derived figure implying closer to 6g/tsp) — presented as a real, honestly wide range rather than a single number this session couldn't actually converge on, not a confident precise figure.

metadata.commonName: flaky sea salt, finishing salt (e.g. Maldon)
metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-17, closing ROADMAP.md's own long-named 'Salt/pepper crystal/grind size as distinct products' gap — the third, most texturally distinct real salt product this vocabulary names: large, thin, irregular pyramidal flakes (real seawater evaporation product), prized specifically for the CRUNCH they retain rather than dissolving into a dish. isDissolvable: false (explicit, not just omitted, unlike salt.json/kosher_salt.json's true) — a real, deliberate difference: this product is essentially never used the way table/kosher salt are (stirred into a dissolving medium during cooking); it's sprinkled on AFTER, specifically to be felt, not dissolved.
metadata.usageNote: Real technique almost universally uses this as a FINISHING salt — sprinkled on a completed dish (data/actions/salt.json's own timing parameter would realistically only ever be 'after_cooking' for this entity, though nothing in this schema enforces that restriction; a real, named, deliberately unenforced gap, the same depth limit every other categorical technique fact in this vocabulary already has) — not a during-cooking seasoning or a brine/dissolving-medium ingredient the way salt.json/kosher_salt.json commonly are.
